Bicycles don't just coast; they actively shift their momentum.

This is achieved by a mechanism that allows the wheel to continue rotating while the pedals are stationary.





This simplest freewheel device consists of two saw-toothed, spring-loaded discs pressing against each other axially with the toothed sides together, like a ratchet but with the usual stationary part also rotating.





When the drive disc slows down or stops rotating, the teeth of the driven disc slip over the drive disc teeth, continuing to rotate and producing a characteristic clicking sound proportionate to the speed difference between the driven gear and the driving gear.
